-- Look up only the products in this order. Always returns exactly one row.
select coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(p)), '[]'::jsonb) as products
from products p
where p.id in (select jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb));

-- Customer history for returning-customer + duplicate checks. Always returns one row.
select
  count(*) filter (where order_status <> 'INCOMPLETE')::int                       as previous_orders,
  count(*) filter (where payment_status = 'PAYMENT_CONFIRMED')::int               as paid_orders,
  coalesce(sum(total_amount) filter (where payment_status = 'PAYMENT_CONFIRMED'), 0)::float8 as lifetime_paid,
  count(*) filter (where items_signature = $2
                     and order_status <> 'INCOMPLETE'
                     and created_at > now() - interval '10 minutes')::int         as recent_duplicates,
  (array_agg(customer_phone order by created_at desc)
     filter (where order_status <> 'INCOMPLETE'))[1]                              as last_phone
from orders
where $1 <> '' and lower(customer_email) = lower($1);

-- Saves the order + its items in one transaction (see create_order in schema.sql)
select * from create_order($1::jsonb);

parameters.content:
## 1. Receive & clean
Webhook (protected by a secret header) → tidy the input.

## 2. Look up facts
Prices + stock from the database, never from the browser. Customer history for duplicate / returning checks.

## 3. Apply business rules
Validation, totals, 5% bonus (≥ ₦500k), review checks, tags, order reference. Deterministic code only.

## 4. Save → respond → notify
Valid and review orders share one path; the message wording differs. Email/Telegram failures never block the order.

## 5. Incomplete orders
Still saved (audit trail), website shows what to fix, team is alerted.
